purpose: Instantiate a reusable inspectable project recipe through strict single-pass placeholders, then retain and ground the resulting creation without inventing or silently rewriting the supplied perspective.

properties.template: object with non-empty id, version, project_type, and files mapping; placeholders use [[AXM:name]]
properties.variables: object mapping every referenced placeholder name to exact raw text
properties.publish_mode: grounded-draft by default; validated when failed checks must block publication

relationships.target: inspectable candidate next-body source outside the active machine body

anatomy_refs.basis: This capability gives the code-template component a bounded live meaning: strict named placeholders in file paths and UTF-8 contents are instantiated once through exact raw text substitution, with missing, unused, malformed, colliding, and unsafe results rejected explicitly.
Rendered files are handed to the existing transactional project publication and grounding machinery.

limitations: substitution is raw exact text and is not parser-aware
templates or callers must supply grammar-specific escaping
loops, conditionals, recursive expansion, binary assets, and semantic code generation are not implemented
self-candidate-project can create inspectable next-body source but does not silently adopt it into the live machine
grounding checks expose observed limits but do not prove runtime behavior or visual quality

truth.basis: The exact placeholder grammar, rendered paths, variables used, single-pass behavior, validation results, gaps, and limitations remain visible.

agency.basis: Humans or AIs supply the template, perspective, values, destination, checks, and strictness; the machine performs no hidden creative rewrite.

continuity.basis: Reusable recipes preserve prior creative structure, project replacement remains transactional, and imperfect new creations may remain available as grounded drafts.

wisdom-before-speed.basis: The capability adds one inspectable reusable primitive and reuses existing project machinery instead of claiming general code generation prematurely.
